meta.title: Mandai: Bird Paradise, Singapore Zoo and the Night Safari | Five Foot Way
meta.description: The wildlife parks on the edge of the central forest: how to see Bird Paradise, the zoo and the Night Safari without spending all day in the sun.

hero.title: Mandai
hero.sub: Bird Paradise, the zoo, the river park and the Night Safari, beside the reservoir at the edge of the central forest.

info.label: Best hours
info.value: Zoo at opening; Night Safari after dark

info.label: Time needed
info.value: A full day, or one park plus the evening

intro.heading: Four parks at the forest's edge
text: Mandai sits on the northern shore of the Upper Seletar Reservoir, bordered by the Central Catchment Nature Reserve. The Singapore Zoo opened here in 1973 with an approach that was unusual at the time: moats and landscaping instead of bars, under a forest canopy. The Night Safari followed, then River Wonders, then Bird Paradise, which moved here from the west of the island in 2023.

It is a big outing. Choose one daytime park and the Night Safari rather than trying to see everything. The zoo and Bird Paradise are best right at opening, when the animals are active and the paths are cool.

rows.title: Bird Paradise
text: Large walk-through aviaries, each landscaped as a region of the world, from a Southeast Asian rainforest to an African wetland. Many paths are covered, which helps in the heat and the rain.

rows.title: Singapore Zoo
text: Under the old trees by the reservoir, the zoo is one of the shadier day outings in Singapore. Arrive at opening, start with the primates and the free-ranging orangutans, and move indoors or to the covered areas after midday.

rows.title: Night Safari
text: A park opened only after dark, with a tram ride and walking trails through habitats lit like moonlight. It is popular and crowded at opening; arrive a little later in the evening for shorter queues. Flash photography is not allowed.

rows.title: River Wonders and the boardwalk
text: River Wonders is largely indoors and air-conditioned, a good refuge from a storm. The Mandai Boardwalk, which runs along the edge of the forest, is free and open to everyone.

bleed.title: The Mandai boardwalk
bleed.text: A short, free boardwalk along the edge of the forest at Mandai, good for an hour before the Night Safari opens.

eat.title: Plan meals around the parks
text: There are restaurants and food courts inside the parks, convenient but busy at lunchtime. For a better meal, eat in the city before an evening visit.

items.name: Inside the parks
items.text: Food courts and restaurants in each park.

items.name: Khatib and Yishun
items.text: Neighbourhood hawker centres near the shuttle bus stop.

items.name: Evenings
items.text: Have an early dinner in town, then arrive at the Night Safari after the first rush.

faq.q: Can I visit more than one park in a day?
a: Yes, and combined tickets are sold. The most comfortable plan is one daytime park in the morning, a rest in the afternoon, and the Night Safari after dark.
Each park has its own hours, and the Night Safari opens only in the evening. Hours change for holidays and events, so confirm them on the Mandai website before you go.
The Mandai Khatib shuttle runs from Khatib MRT on the North-South Line. A taxi from the city takes about half an hour.
